_comment: PROJECT-WIDE MCP config. Loaded automatically by every editor (Cursor/VSCode)
Claude session in this workspace, and merged into any CLI session launched
WITHOUT --strict-mcp-config.
It deliberately contains NO robot-backend servers. Each of those spawns a ROS
node with a FIXED name (robot_backend_motion_mcp_server, watchdog_node, ...),
so every additional editor window created a second node with the same name.
Observed 2026-08-31: two Cursor sessions -> duplicate /watchdog_node,
/robot_backend_motion_mcp_server, /robot_backend_scene_mcp_server and
/robot_backend_gripper_mcp_server, with ros2's 'nodes in the graph that share
an exact name' warning. Two watchdog nodes can both arm monitors and record
verdicts, and both sets append to the same mcp_calls_*.jsonl in the session
dir, so a scored run's action trace interleaves two sessions.
RUN.md already forbids scored runs from editor sessions for this reason. The
sanctioned entry points are the per-role configs, launched explicitly:
claude --mcp-config watchdog.mcp.json --strict-mcp-config
claude --mcp-config executor.mcp.json --strict-mcp-config
Keeping the robot-backend servers here bought nothing those two do not, and
cost a duplicate ROS node per open window.
kit stays: it is a TCP bridge to the running Isaac Sim (omni.kit.mcp on
OMNI_KIT_MCP_PORT) and creates no ROS node, so N editor windows cause no
graph collisions. It is also read-only-by-default and useful for inspecting
the stage while authoring.
If a session needs live read-only observation of the cell, add an
observer.mcp.json with only the query tools and launch it explicitly with
--strict-mcp-config -- do not reintroduce command servers here.
